data.name: Dwimalu
data.gender_notes: Dwimalu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Dwimalu is derived from Sanskrit, meaning 'two hands of Lord Shiva'. This name is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology, representing the divine and powerful presence of Shiva. It is believed that those named Dwimalu are blessed with the strength and wisdom of the lord. The name Dwimalu carries the meaning “Two hands of Lord Shiva” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dwimalu usually hope their child will grow to embody two hands of lord shiva and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Dwimalu is believed to be associated with the goddesses of motherhood and nourishment, and is said to bring blessings of abundance and protection.
data.etymology: Dwimalu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Two hands of Lord Shiva.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dwimalu total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dwimalu is a reflection of the richness and diversity of Hindu culture. It represents the deep reverence and devotion towards Lord Shiva, a central deity in Hinduism. This name is not only a personal identity but also a symbol of the spiritual and cultural heritage of the Hindu community.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Lord Shiva is often depicted with two hands, each holding a symbol representing creation and destruction. The name Dwimalu signifies the unity and balance of these two aspects, as well as the realization of the divine presence within oneself. Those named Dwimalu are believed to embody the strength, wisdom, and power of Lord Shiva, making them spiritual beings in their own right.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dwimalu signifies the one who carries the dual aspects of wisdom and ignorance within. The number two symbolizes the balance between these two states, emphasizing the importance of discernment and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Dwimala was a queen who ruled the Andhra Kingdom in 5th and 6th century AD. She is considered to be one of the most powerful and revered rulers of the Andhra Dynasty. Her reign was marked by peace, prosperity, and architectural advancements, particularly in the field of Buddhist art and architecture.
historical_references.context: Andhra Kingdom, Buddhist art and architecture, powerful and revered ruler

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Dwimala is found in the Jataka Tales, a collection of Buddhist stories. In one of the tales, King Dwimala is portrayed as a just and virtuous ruler who upholds the Buddhist Dharma and ensures peace and prosperity in his kingdom.
